new.title: Pay respects at Anıtkabir, Atatürk's mausoleum
new.desc: Anıtkabir is the monumental tomb of Mustafa Kemal Atatürk, founder of the Turkish Republic, on Anıttepe hill. Designed by Emin Onat and Orhan Arda and completed in 1953, it is approached along the Lion Road and centres on a vast ceremonial plaza.
new.tip: Entry is free but bags are screened; allow two to three hours and bring ID. Take the metro to Tandoğan and walk about 10 minutes uphill.
new.q: Anıtkabir, Çankaya, Ankara

new.title: Explore the Anıtkabir Museum and War of Independence displays
new.desc: Beneath the Anıtkabir plaza, the museum shows Atatürk's personal belongings, gifts, books and cars, along with a War of Independence section with dioramas and a short film. The complex is among the most visited sites in Turkey.
new.tip: Enter via the side doors of the plaza; the museum is free. Visit in the morning when queues at the mausoleum are shorter.
new.q: Anıtkabir Müzesi, Anıttepe, Çankaya, Ankara

new.title: Stroll through the Peace Park below Anıtkabir
new.desc: Barış Parkı, the Peace Park, surrounds Anıtkabir with trees from many countries that were planted as gifts when the mausoleum was built. Paths run beneath the hill and give a calm contrast to the formal tomb above.
new.tip: Combine with a visit to Anıtkabir; the park is free to enter. Good for a shaded walk on hot days.
new.q: Barış Parkı, Anıttepe, Çankaya, Ankara

new.title: See Kocatepe Mosque, Ankara's largest mosque
new.desc: Kocatepe Mosque in Kızılay was built between 1967 and 1987 in the style of classical Ottoman mosques, with four 88-metre minarets and a central dome. It is among the largest mosques in Turkey and holds a shopping centre in its basement.
new.tip: Visit outside prayer times and dress modestly; scarves are provided. The area around it is lively in the evening.
new.q: Kocatepe Camii, Kocatepe Mahallesi, Çankaya, Ankara

new.title: Visit Güvenpark and the Confidence Monument
new.desc: Güvenpark is a small central park in Kızılay, home to the Güvenlik Anıtı (Security or Confidence Monument) erected in 1935 and a favourite meeting point. The relief on the monument stresses the Republic's reliance on security and the rule of law.
new.tip: Sit by the fountains for people-watching; it sits right at the Kızılay metro exit. Busiest at lunch and after work.
new.q: Güvenpark, Kızılay, Çankaya, Ankara

new.title: Cross Kızılay Square, Ankara's city centre
new.desc: Kızılay takes its name from the Turkish Red Crescent (Kızılay), which once had its headquarters there, and has been Ankara's commercial and social centre since the 1920s. The square joins Atatürk Boulevard with the busy shopping streets of Sakarya, Konur and Meşrutiyet.
new.tip: Come on a weekend evening for the crowds and street musicians. Use the Kızılay metro interchange as your starting point.
new.q: Kızılay Meydanı, Kızılay, Çankaya, Ankara

new.title: Find the Human Rights Monument on Yüksel Caddesi
new.desc: The Human Rights Monument on Yüksel Caddesi is a pedestrian-street sculpture in Kızılay that has become a symbol of civil protest and gatherings in Ankara. The street around it is lined with cafés, bookstalls and street performers.
new.tip: Walk the pedestrianised Yüksel Caddesi between Kızılay and Tunalı for street life. It is free and open at all times.
new.q: İnsan Hakları Anıtı, Yüksel Caddesi, Kızılay, Çankaya, Ankara

new.title: See the Hatti Sun Disc Monument in Sıhhiye Square
new.desc: The Hatti Sun Disc stands in Sıhhiye Square, installed in 1978 and based on a bronze standard unearthed at Alacahöyük, a Bronze Age Hattian site. It has become a symbol of Ankara and appears in the municipal emblem.
new.tip: Best photographed from the Sıhhiye metro exit; it sits in the middle of a very busy traffic circle, so use the underpass.
new.q: Sıhhiye Meydanı Hitit Güneş Kursu Anıtı, Sıhhiye, Çankaya, Ankara

new.title: Browse contemporary art at CerModern
new.desc: CerModern is a contemporary arts centre in a restored 1920s railway workshop complex near Sıhhiye. It hosts rotating exhibitions, concerts and workshops and is run by the Ankara metropolitan municipality.
new.tip: Entry to most exhibitions is free; check the programme online and visit on weekdays for quiet halls.
new.q: CerModern, Altınsoy Caddesi, Sıhhiye, Ankara

new.title: Tour the Grand National Assembly of Turkey
new.desc: The Turkish parliament building at Bakanlıklar was designed by Clemens Holzmeister and opened in 1960 after decades of construction. Its distinctive architecture and large grounds are part of Ankara's government quarter, with guided visits arranged for visitors.
new.tip: Visits need advance booking through the Assembly's visitor service and photo ID; check the official site for tour days.
new.q: Türkiye Büyük Millet Meclisi, Bakanlıklar, Çankaya, Ankara

new.title: Walk through Saraçoğlu Quarter's Republic-era houses
new.desc: The Saraçoğlu Quarter in Kızılay was built between 1944 and 1946, usually credited to architect Paul Bonatz, as housing for civil servants. It is often described as the Republic's first mass-housing project and has been restored after years of dispute.
new.tip: The restored grounds are open as a green public space; go in daylight and combine with a walk to Kızılay.
new.q: Saraçoğlu Mahallesi, Kızılay, Çankaya, Ankara

new.title: Visit the Haritacılık Müzesi, the military mapping museum
new.desc: The Mapping Museum in Cebeci, run by the General Command of Mapping, displays survey instruments, historic maps and cartographic tools. It is one of the museums listed among Ankara's specialist collections.
new.tip: It is on a military site, so bring ID and check opening days and visiting rules in advance.
new.q: Haritacılık Müzesi, Harita Genel Komutanlığı, Cebeci, Ankara

new.title: See the Faculty of Language, History and Geography
new.desc: The Dil ve Tarih-Coğrafya Fakültesi near Sıhhiye was founded in 1935 on Atatürk's initiative to study Turkish language, history and geography. Its historic building is a landmark of Ankara University.
new.tip: Public access to courtyards is usually possible on weekdays; ask at the entrance before photographing.
new.q: Ankara Üniversitesi Dil ve Tarih-Coğrafya Fakültesi, Sıhhiye, Ankara

new.title: See the Mülkiye building of Ankara University
new.desc: The Faculty of Political Sciences, known as Mülkiye, occupies a 1930s modernist building in Cebeci by Swiss-Austrian architect Ernst Egli. It trained generations of Turkish civil servants and diplomats.
new.tip: Walk the Cebeci campus on weekdays; interior access depends on the faculty.
new.q: Ankara Üniversitesi Siyasal Bilgiler Fakültesi, Cebeci, Ankara

new.title: Jog or picnic in Kurtuluş Park
new.desc: Kurtuluş Park lies in the Fidanlık quarter of Çankaya, on the site of a former tree nursery, with walking tracks, playgrounds and a pool. Ankaray's Kurtuluş station is beside it.
new.tip: Free and open all day; busiest on weekend afternoons. Reach it by Ankaray to Kurtuluş.
new.q: Kurtuluş Parkı, Çankaya, Ankara

new.title: See an art-house film at Büyülü Fener Kızılay
new.desc: Büyülü Fener opened in Kızılay in 2005 as a cinema and culture centre with several screens. It is known for independent and festival films and hosts the Başka Sinema programme.
new.tip: Check the weekly schedule and arrive early for festival screenings; it is on Meşrutiyet Caddesi at Hatay Sokak.
new.q: Büyülü Fener Kızılay Sineması, Meşrutiyet Caddesi, Hatay Sokak 18, Çankaya, Ankara

new.title: Catch a play at Akün Sahnesi
new.desc: Akün Sahnesi is a State Theatres stage in Kızılay, opened in 2002 on the site of the former Akün cinema. It stages mainstream and classic plays in Turkish.
new.tip: Book through the State Theatres site or Biletinial. Plays are in Turkish, so check the programme.
new.q: Akün Sahnesi, Kızılay, Çankaya, Ankara

new.title: Browse Dost Kitabevi, a Kızılay bookshop institution
new.desc: Dost Kitabevi on Atatürk Bulvarı carries a wide range of Turkish and foreign-language books for academic and general readers. It frequently hosts author events and signings.
new.tip: Ask about upcoming author events; the staff know their stock well.
new.q: Dost Kitabevi, Atatürk Bulvarı, Kızılay, Çankaya, Ankara

new.title: Browse İmge Kitabevi on Konur Sokak
new.desc: İmge Kitabevi is a long-running bookshop on Konur Sokak in Kızılay, known for social sciences, arts, humanities and political titles. It is a staple of the street's student and academic crowd.
new.tip: Konur Sokak is pedestrian; combine with a coffee at one of the nearby book cafés.
new.q: İmge Kitabevi, Konur Sokak, Kızılay, Çankaya, Ankara

new.title: Browse English books at Mephisto Kitabevi in Bahçelievler
new.desc: The Bahçelievler branch of Mephisto Kitabevi has an extensive English-language section and a café area. It is a favoured stop for expats, students and readers of foreign-language fiction.
new.tip: Come in the evening for a coffee after browsing; located near the 7. Cadde area.
new.q: Mephisto Kitabevi, Bahçelievler, Çankaya, Ankara

new.title: Spend an evening on Sakarya Caddesi
new.desc: Sakarya Caddesi in Kızılay is the city's classic student-and-office nightlife street, with bars, pubs, kebab shops and cafés. Rock bars and small live music venues cluster here and on the side streets.
new.tip: Weekend nights are busiest; start with a döner or fish meal and move on to a bar.
new.q: Sakarya Caddesi, Kızılay, Çankaya, Ankara

new.title: Wander pedestrian Konur Sokak for books and cafés
new.desc: Konur Sokak is a pedestrian street in Kızılay lined with bookshops, tea houses and cafés, including several book cafés with bohemian atmospheres. It is a favourite with students and writers.
new.tip: Go in the afternoon for second-hand books and coffee; it is a short walk from Kızılay square.
new.q: Konur Sokak, Meşrutiyet Mahallesi, Çankaya, Ankara

new.title: Hear live Turkish rock at Nil Bar
new.desc: Nil Bar on Bayındır 1 Sokak is a long-standing live music venue in Kızılay with Turkish rock bands. It is among the places listed for Ankara's rock bar scene.
new.tip: Live sets start late; check social media for the lineup. Hours and programme may change.
new.q: Nil Bar, Bayındır 1 Sokak, Kızılay, Çankaya, Ankara

new.title: Eat charcoal döner at Cici Piknik
new.desc: Cici Piknik has served meat-only charcoal döner on Kumrular Caddesi in Kızılay since 1984. It is one of Ankara's old-style döner stands, a tiny shop serving bread or lavash wraps without mince.
new.tip: Order döner in a lavash wrap and eat it standing or at the few seats; it is crowded at lunch.
new.q: Cici Piknik, Kumrular Caddesi 8, Kızılay, Çankaya, Ankara

new.title: Sit down at Göksu Lokantası for classic home cooking
new.desc: Göksu Lokantası on Bayındır-1 Sokak keeps an old-Ankara atmosphere with 1970s-80s decor and a large dining room. It is a regular for politicians, businesspeople and families.
new.tip: Try the traditional stews and grills; lunch gets busy with office workers.
new.q: Göksu Lokantası, Bayındır 1 Sokak 22, Kızılay, Çankaya, Ankara

new.title: Try spicy Urfa kebab at Urfalı Hayrağ'ın Yeri
new.desc: Urfalı Hayrağ'ın Yeri on Bayındır 1 Sokak serves spicy Urfa-style kebabs and is a good option around Kızılay. The menu centres on adana and urfa kebabs with Southeast Turkish sides.
new.tip: Order the Urfa kebab with onions and sumac; it is lunch-and-dinner only.
new.q: Urfalı Hayrağ'ın Yeri, Bayındır 1 Sokak 9/B, Kızılay, Çankaya, Ankara

new.title: Drink beer with kalamar at Net Piknik on Sakarya
new.desc: Net Piknik is a very casual spot on Sakarya Caddesi that reflects the spirit of the street. Suggested dishes are Arnavut ciğeri and kalamar, often paired with beer or rakı.
new.tip: Go in the evening for the atmosphere; reviewers say food is simple.
new.q: Net Piknik, Sakarya Caddesi, Kızılay, Çankaya, Ankara

new.title: Eat döner at Ankara Meydan Döner
new.desc: Ankara Meydan Döner on Fevzi Çakmak-2 Sokak is listed among the best döner in Kızılay. Döner here is served in bread or on a plate in the Ankara style.
new.tip: Choose a plate with pilaf for lunch; expect queues at midday.
new.q: Ankara Meydan Döner, Fevzi Çakmak 2 Sokak 40, Kızılay, Çankaya, Ankara

new.title: Have tripe soup at Rumeli İşkembecisi, open 24 hours
new.desc: Rumeli İşkembecisi on Bayındır-1 Sokak serves lentil, tripe and trotter soups round the clock. It is a classic after-night-out stop in Kızılay.
new.tip: Order işkembe soup with garlic and vinegar; it is open 24 hours.
new.q: Rumeli İşkembecisi, Bayındır 1 Sokak 25/A, Kızılay, Çankaya, Ankara

new.title: Have breakfast at Baykuş Cafe on Konur Sokak
new.desc: Baykuş Cafe on Konur Sokak serves breakfast and brunch with serpme and single plates, menemen and toast in a bohemian setting. It sits among the street's book-and-coffee spots.
new.tip: Go on a weekend morning for serpme kahvaltı; seating fills quickly.
new.q: Baykuş Cafe, Konur Sokak 8/3, Meşrutiyet, Çankaya, Ankara

new.title: Order cheese gözleme at Zaytung Zone
new.desc: Zaytung Zone on Konur Sokak serves cheese gözleme, fruit pancakes and omelets, and a two-person breakfast with menemen and börek. It is part of the street's café scene.
new.tip: Share the two-person breakfast; go before noon.
new.q: Zaytung Zone, Konur Sokak 8, Meşrutiyet, Çankaya, Ankara

new.title: Read over tea at Kitapça Bayındır book café
new.desc: Kitapça Bayındır on Bayındır-2 Sokak is a book café with breakfast plates, snacks and tea and a backyard where cats wander. It is popular with students and readers.
new.tip: Come for tea and a toast with a book; the courtyard is pleasant in spring.
new.q: Kitapça Bayındır, Bayındır 2 Sokak 50/A, Kocatepe, Çankaya, Ankara

new.title: Order breakfast at Mekan Kafe Kitab & Kahve
new.desc: Mekan Kafe Kitab & Kahve on Atatürk Bulvarı is a book café with full breakfast plates, solo portions, menemen and toast.
new.tip: Solo breakfast plates suit one diner; open mornings through the evening.
new.q: Mekan Kafe Kitab ve Kahve, Atatürk Bulvarı 88, Kızılay, Çankaya, Ankara

new.title: Try dibek coffee and crêpes at Kahve Geleneği
new.desc: Kahve Geleneği on Selanik Caddesi serves serpme breakfast and crêpes along with menengiç and dibek coffee, two traditional Anatolian coffee styles.
new.tip: Order dibek or menengiç coffee after a crêpe; Selanik Caddesi is busy in the afternoon.
new.q: Kahve Geleneği, Selanik Caddesi 26/B, Meşrutiyet, Çankaya, Ankara

new.title: Eat Akçaabat köfte at Hamzaoğlu on Selanik Caddesi
new.desc: Hamzaoğlu Akçaabat Köfte & Balık & Kahvaltı Salonu on Selanik Caddesi offers Black Sea style Akçaabat köfte and fish plus traditional breakfast.
new.tip: Order the köfte with piyaz or a fish plate; it also serves breakfast.
new.q: Hamzaoğlu Akçaabat Köfte Balık Kahvaltı Salonu, Selanik Caddesi 50, Çankaya, Ankara

new.title: Pick savory pastries at Divan Pastanesi Kızılay
new.desc: Divan Pastanesi's Kızılay branch on Atatürk Bulvarı offers pastries and savory pastries with tea, a lighter option than a full serpme breakfast.
new.tip: Try the poğaça and börek with tea in the morning.
new.q: Divan Pastanesi, Atatürk Bulvarı 58, Kızılay, Çankaya, Ankara

new.title: Eat potato toast at Çatı Cafe above Sakarya Caddesi
new.desc: Çatı Cafe on Sakarya Caddesi is a budget-friendly café with a balcony over the street, known for potato toast, menemen and simple breakfast plates.
new.tip: Take a balcony table for street views; arrive early at weekends.
new.q: Çatı Cafe, Sakarya Caddesi 8, Kızılay, Çankaya, Ankara

new.title: Buy Turkish sweets at Ali Uzun Şekercilik
new.desc: Ali Uzun Şekercilik on İnkılap Sokak in Kızılay is cited as one of Ankara's oldest confectioners, selling Turkish delight, candies and sweets.
new.tip: Pick a mixed box of lokum and candies as a gift.
new.q: Ali Uzun Şekercilik, İnkılap Sokak 13, Kızılay, Çankaya, Ankara

new.title: Drink rakı at Necmi Usta'nın Yeri meyhane
new.desc: Necmi Usta'nın Yeri is a family-run meyhane in a passage near Strazburg Caddesi on the Maltepe side, known for ciğer and pazı sarması.
new.tip: Order the liver and chard rolls with rakı; arrive early for a seat.
new.q: Necmi Usta'nın Yeri, Strazburg Caddesi, Maltepe, Çankaya, Ankara

new.title: Eat meze and kebab at Çukurağa Sofrası in Emek
new.desc: Çukurağa Sofrası on Bosna Hersek Caddesi in Emek is known for kebab with an emphasis on meze and service.
new.tip: Start with a meze plate and share kebabs.
new.q: Çukurağa Sofrası, Bosna Hersek Caddesi 22, Emek, Çankaya, Ankara

new.title: Eat cağ kebap at Metin Usta in Emek
new.desc: Metin Usta Cağ Kebap on Bişkek Caddesi in Emek serves cağ kebap, thin horizontal-spit lamb sliced onto skewers in Erzurum style.
new.tip: Order several skewers with lavash and onions.
new.q: Metin Usta Cağ Kebap, Bişkek Caddesi 23, Emek, Çankaya, Ankara

new.title: Eat traditional Turkish dishes at Yıldız Aspava Emek
new.desc: Yıldız Aspava in Emek is a well-known traditional Turkish restaurant, part of the Aspava family of Ankara grill restaurants.
new.tip: Order a mixed grill and ayran; good for families.
new.q: Yıldız Aspava, Emek, Çankaya, Ankara

new.title: Taste old-machine ice cream at Hatun Pastanesi
new.desc: Hatun Pastanesi on 65. Sokak near 7. Cadde in Bahçelievler is cited for ice cream made on decades-old machines, alongside classic cakes and pastries.
new.tip: Try the ice cream first, then a slice of cake.
new.q: Hatun Pastanesi, 65. Sokak 3/B, Bahçelievler, Çankaya, Ankara

new.title: Have croissants at La Lune Patisserie in Bahçelievler
new.desc: La Lune Patisserie on Oğuzhan Asiltürk Caddesi in Yukarı Bahçelievler is known for cakes, croissants and coffee.
new.tip: Go in the morning for fresh croissants.
new.q: La Lune Patisserie, Oğuzhan Asiltürk Caddesi 22A, Bahçelievler, Çankaya, Ankara

new.title: Sit at Académie Café on Bahçelievler's 7. Cadde
new.desc: Académie is a café at the start of Aşkabat Caddesi, known as 7. Cadde, Bahçelievler's long-standing café and dining strip.
new.tip: Come in the evening when the street is busy.
new.q: Académie Café, Aşkabat Caddesi 1, Bahçelievler, Çankaya, Ankara

new.title: Drink craft beer at The Bigos gastropub
new.desc: The Bigos is a gastropub on 6. Cadde in Bahçelievler, among the best-reviewed venues of the area.
new.tip: Order a local craft beer and a burger; booking helps on weekends.
new.q: The Bigos, 6. Cadde, Bahçelievler, Çankaya, Ankara

new.title: Catch a concert at Nergiz Gösteri Merkezi in Kızılay
new.desc: Nergiz Gösteri Merkezi is an events venue in central Kızılay hosting concerts and shows listed on ticket platforms.
new.tip: Check the programme and book via iTicket; hours vary by event.
new.q: Nergiz Gösteri Merkezi, Kızılay, Çankaya, Ankara

new.title: Hear acoustic and folk sets at Adres Bar
new.desc: Adres Bar on Bayındır Sokak is a Kızılay live venue, varying from traditional folk music to acoustic sets and modern rock.
new.tip: Evening sets; check the programme as hours and acts change.
new.q: Adres Bar, Bayındır Sokak, Kızılay, Çankaya, Ankara

new.title: Stroll Bahçelievler's 7. Cadde for cafés and shops
new.desc: 7. Cadde, officially Aşkabat Caddesi, is Bahçelievler's popular street of cafés, restaurants and shops, a long-standing local hangout.
new.tip: Go on a summer evening when the terraces are full.
new.q: 7. Cadde, Aşkabat Caddesi, Bahçelievler, Çankaya, Ankara
